keepers-carousel.pitch: A hand-painted carousel of sea creatures, under cover in the middle of the plaza.
description: The carousel has been turning since opening day. Its animals are seahorses, pelicans and one very large turtle, and the roof makes it a reliable stop when the afternoon rain comes through.

plaza-lantern-theater.pitch: The park's indoor stage, with a 25-minute show several times a day.
description: The theater opened in 2003 and seats a big crowd in the air conditioning. The current show tells the story of the first keeper of El Faro with music, puppetry and a great many lanterns.
tips: Showtimes are posted at the theater doors each morning.

the-lantern-keepers-tale.pitch: A slow ride through the story the whole park is built on.
description: Boats shaped like lanterns carry you through nine minutes of scenes: the storm, the shipwreck and the keeper who lit the first lamp. It is dark in places but never frightening, and there is no height requirement.
tips: This is one of the rides included in Paso Rapido.

abuelas-flying-kites.pitch: Kites that lift and dip in a wide circle above the village rooftops.
description: Each kite seats a child and an adult, and the rider in front controls how high it flies. The ride is short and outdoors, so it pauses when lightning is in the area.

cuentos-puppet-playhouse.pitch: An 18-minute puppet show in a small theater that smells like sawdust and paint.
description: The playhouse joined the village in 1999. The puppeteers work in full view and change the story with the seasons, and the front rows are saved for children sitting on the floor.

little-skiffs.pitch: Tiny boats on a winding canal, steered by whoever grabs the wheel first.
description: The skiffs follow a track under the water, so nobody can get lost, but every boat has a wheel and a bell. It is a first ride for a lot of toddlers. It runs outdoors and closes when storms are near.

firefly-flight.pitch: A family coaster that swoops through the treetops, at its best after dark.
description: Firefly Flight is fast enough to count and gentle enough to try again. Riders need to be 40 inches tall. At night the trains trail light through the canopy, which is why the line gets longer after sunset.

lumina-grove-walk.pitch: A footpath through the glowing forest, taken at whatever pace you like.
description: The walk is about fifteen minutes if you do not stop, and most people stop. The path is flat and wide enough for strollers and wheelchairs, and the lights respond when you step on the marked stones.

glowworm-caverns.pitch: An indoor boat ride through caves lit only by what lives on the ceiling.
description: Eight quiet minutes underground, in the coolest air in the park. The boats drift past pools, a waterfall you pass behind and a last cavern where the whole roof is alive with light.

song-of-the-sirena.pitch: The original mermaid dark ride, with a melody people hum for the rest of the day.
description: Clamshell cars glide under the surface of the bay and through the sirena's grotto. The ride dates from the park's first season and has been restored more than once without changing the song.

pearl-diver-spin.pitch: Spinning diving bells that rise, tilt and come back down.
description: A step up from the carousel and a step down from the coasters. Riders need to be 36 inches tall, and the bells spin faster if everyone inside leans the same way.

tidepool-splash-garden.pitch: Fountains, jets and shallow pools for getting soaked without leaving the park.
description: The splash garden is open play with no line and no time limit. There are changing rooms next door, and the jets run on a pattern the older kids learn to predict.
tips: Bring a towel and a change of shirt.

sirena-lagoon-spectacular.pitch: The evening show on the lagoon, with fountains, boats and light on the water.
description: The spectacular runs about 22 minutes and is best seen from the lagoon wall or from a window table at The Pearl Table. It has been the park's closing show since 2010.
tips: The viewing wall fills about half an hour before the show.

galleon-run.pitch: A family coaster that races a pirate ship through the harbor.
description: Galleon Run was the first coaster built on the island. It is three minutes of quick turns around the masts and warehouses of the port, with one drop that gets a scream out of most first-timers. Riders must be 42 inches tall.

smugglers-tide.pitch: An indoor flume through the smugglers' caves, with a splashdown at the end.
description: Boats climb in the dark, drift past the smugglers' hoard and come down a drop into the harbor. You will get wet, how wet depends on your row. Riders must be 40 inches tall.
tips: The front row gets the worst of it.

harbor-bumper-boats.pitch: Bumper boats with water cannons, in a walled corner of the harbor.
description: Each boat holds one or two riders and has a cannon on the bow. Drivers need to be 44 inches tall. Nobody stays dry, including people watching from the dock.

mercado-players.pitch: Street theater in the market square, fifteen minutes at a time.
description: The players perform on an open stage among the stalls, with sword fights, bad jokes and a volunteer from the crowd. There are no seats, so find a spot along the fountain.

cloudskimmer.pitch: Gliders on long arms that swing out over the edge of the land.
description: Riders steer their own wing left and right as the ride lifts and turns. It is outdoors, breezy and a good test of whether someone is ready for the coaster next door. The height requirement is 38 inches.

starfall-tower.pitch: An indoor drop tower that falls through a sky full of stars.
description: The tower rises slowly in the dark, pauses, and drops. Then it does it again from a different height. Being indoors, it runs in any weather. Riders must be 42 inches tall.

constellation-coaster.pitch: A coaster in the dark, and the most intense ride in Costa Encandela.
description: Constellation Coaster launches through a field of stars with turns you cannot see coming. It is entirely indoors, which keeps it open through storms and makes the line long on rainy days. Riders must be 46 inches tall.
tips: Ride it first thing or during the evening show.

tradewind-swings.pitch: Chair swings that lift out over the water at the end of the pier.
description: A classic, set where the view is best. The swings rise high enough to see the whole park and tilt as they turn. Riders must be 44 inches tall.

pier-wheel.pitch: An eight-minute turn on the wheel, with the Gulf on one side and the coasters on the other.
description: The Pier Wheel is the one ride in Punta Tormenta with no height requirement, and the best way to plan the rest of the day. The gondolas are open to the breeze, so it stops for lightning.

stormwatch-stunt-show.pitch: High dives, jet skis and controlled explosions in the arena at the end of the pier.
description: The stunt show runs about 24 minutes and has played here since 2008. The first four rows are marked as the splash zone, and the marking is accurate.
tips: Showtimes are posted at the arena gate.

riptide-racer.pitch: A launched coaster that runs the length of the wharf and back.
description: Riptide Racer opened in 2009 and gave the wharf its second big ride. It is two fast minutes with a launch instead of a lift hill. Riders must be 52 inches tall.

the-anvil.pitch: The drop tower. Up slowly, down very fast.
description: The Anvil has been the landmark of Punta Tormenta since opening day in 2004. Seats face outward, the climb takes long enough to think about it, and the drop does not. Riders must be 52 inches tall.

cargo-crane-chaos.pitch: A swinging, spinning crane arm with riders on the end of it.
description: The arm swings higher on each pass while the gondola turns, so you never face the same way twice. It looks worse from the ground than it feels. Riders must be 48 inches tall.

foundry-dodgems.pitch: Bumper cars inside the old foundry, with sparks overhead.
description: The dodgems are indoors and open in all weather, which makes them the busiest ride in the park during a storm. Drivers must be 44 inches tall.

el-remolino.pitch: The whirlpool: the coaster Punta Tormenta was built around.
description: El Remolino opened with the park in 2004 and is still its signature. The track coils through the cove in tight spirals with two inversions over the water. Riders must be 54 inches tall.

whirlpool-rapids.pitch: Round rafts on a tumbling river, with no way to tell who gets soaked.
description: Six-seat rafts spin down a course of rapids, waterfalls and one whirlpool. Somebody in every raft ends up drenched. Riders must be 42 inches tall.

backwash-falls.pitch: A flume ride with one big drop and a wave that reaches the bridge.
description: Backwash Falls was added in 2006. The drop is the whole ride, and the bridge at the bottom is there for people who want the wave without the line. Riders must be 44 inches tall.

nimbus-peak.pitch: The tallest coaster on the island, up on the ridge.
description: Nimbus Peak climbs above everything else in the park, then spends three minutes coming down. The first drop is the reason people ride it and the airtime hills are the reason they come back. Riders must be 54 inches tall.

updraft.pitch: A tower that launches upward instead of dropping.
description: Updraft fires riders to the top and lets them float there for a moment before bringing them down. It stands beside Nimbus Peak and gives almost the same view. Riders must be 48 inches tall.

windshear.pitch: A giant pendulum that swings past upside down.
description: Windshear is the most intense flat ride on the island. The arm swings a ring of outward-facing seats higher on each pass until it goes all the way over. Riders must be 54 inches tall.

squall-line.pitch: A family coaster on the ridge, for riders working their way up.
description: Squall Line arrived in 2017 so that the Heights had something for riders at 42 inches. It is quick, smooth and just fast enough to feel like the real thing.

ojo-de-la-tormenta.pitch: Eye of the storm: the newest and biggest coaster on the island.
description: Ojo de la Tormenta opened with Cabo Trueno in 2021. Trains launch out of the research station, circle the storm wall and dive through the eye. It runs three minutes, and riders must be 52 inches tall.

trueno-rally.pitch: An indoor chase in storm-tracker trucks, through wind, rain and worse.
description: Trueno Rally is a five-minute dark ride that moves quickly without being rough. It is indoors, so it stays open when the coasters close. Riders must be 40 inches tall.

tempest-trackers.pitch: Weather balloons for the whole family, with a view of the storm wall.
description: The gentlest ride in Cabo Trueno. Balloon baskets rise, turn and drift for four minutes. Riders must be 36 inches tall, and smaller children can watch from the station deck.

marea-wave-bay.pitch: The wave pool, with a beach entry and swells every few minutes.
description: Marea Wave Bay is shallow at the sand and deep at the wall. A horn sounds before each set of waves. There is no height requirement, and life jackets are free at the hut beside the bay.

rio-perezoso.pitch: The lazy river, a slow loop around the whole beach.
description: Find a tube at any of the three entry points and let the current do the work. One lap takes about 25 minutes, with a waterfall you can steer around if you want to stay dry above the shoulders.

coral-plunge.pitch: A near-freefall body slide from the top of the tower.
description: You step into the capsule, cross your arms and wait. Coral Plunge is over in seconds. Riders must be 48 inches tall.

barracuda-bowl.pitch: A tube slide that drops into a giant bowl and circles the drain.
description: Two-person tubes shoot down a dark tunnel into the bowl, spin around it a few times and drop out through the middle. Riders must be 48 inches tall.

mantaray-racers.pitch: Six lanes, six mats, one finish line.
description: Grab a mat, lie down head first and race the people next to you. A timer at the bottom shows who won. Riders must be 42 inches tall.

eel-tubes.pitch: Twisting tube slides in and out of the dark.
description: The mildest way down from the tower, which is not the same as mild. Single or double tubes. Riders must be 42 inches tall.

hatchling-harbor.pitch: A water play structure with small slides, sprayers and a bucket that tips.
description: Everything here is sized for young children, and the water is ankle deep. The bucket at the top fills and tips every few minutes, with a bell to warn anyone who would prefer to miss it.

little-tides.pitch: A calm, shallow pool for the smallest swimmers.
description: Little Tides has a gentle slope, soft floor and shade over half the pool. Swim diapers are available at the cove entrance.

monzon.pitch: A family raft slide, four riders at a time, down the face of the ridge.
description: Monzon is the slide the whole group can do together. Round rafts swing up the walls of wide open turns for three minutes on the way down. Riders must be 42 inches tall.

cliffdiver.pitch: The steepest slide in the park, straight down the cliff.
description: Cliffdiver is the most intense ride at Playa Zambulla. The floor drops out from under you at the top and the rest takes about four seconds. Riders must be 48 inches tall.

twin-squalls.pitch: Two tube slides side by side, built for racing.
description: Pick a side, pick a partner and go at the same time. The slides cross twice on the way down. Riders must be 48 inches tall.

el-faro-lighthouse-climb.pitch: Walk the spiral stair to the lamp room and see the whole island from the gallery.
description: El Faro is the oldest thing in the park and the reason the park is where it is. The climb is a walk, not a ride: a spiral stair past the keeper's quarters and the old logbooks, up to the lamp room and the open gallery around it.

Take it at your own pace. Most people spend about twenty minutes, longer near sunset when the gallery faces straight into it. There is no height requirement and no line to skip, so it is not part of Paso Rapido.
tips: The stair is outdoors at the top. The gallery stays open in rain but the view goes with the weather.
Go up in the last hour before closing to watch the plaza lanterns come on from above.
